title: Talk 'n Play (CBS Toys)
subtitle: a cassette-and-book desktop toy where the child's own recorded voice becomes part of the program — a microphone plus a music-mixer interaction lets the child add or remove individual instruments from the backing track
why_scout_cares: The Talk 'n Play (1984, CBS Toys/Child Guidance, later Hasbro and Playskool) is an interactive cassette/book reader with a genuinely distinctive interaction model: a microphone and a set of action keys let the child record their own voice into the program so they literally become a voice-actor inside the story, and in music programs they can add or remove individual instruments from the backing track like a miniature audio mixer. It was invented by Michael J. Freeman, who holds a patent on the device. It is a rare kids' toy whose interaction is about recording and mixing rather than drill-and-response, making it a meaningful sibling to the museum's voice- and audio-focused entries.

research.title: Talk 'n Play
research.by: CBS Toys / Child Guidance (later Hasbro / Playskool)
research.overview: The Talk 'n Play (1984) is an interactive cassette/book toy. The child inserts a cassette and opens an accompanying book; a voice on the tape narrates and prompts, and the child responds using a set of buttons plus a microphone. What makes it distinctive is the microphone: the child records their own voice into the program, becoming a participant/voice-actor in the story, and in music programs they can add or remove individual instruments from the backing track — a toy-sized audio mixer. It was invented by Michael J. Freeman, who patented the concept. The brand passed from CBS Toys/Child Guidance to Hasbro and later Playskool.

deepDive.heading: Child-as-voice-actor
deepDive.text: The microphone lets the child record their own voice into the tape-driven program, so the toy stops being a passive playback device and becomes a recording instrument. The child performs their part of the story — a genuinely embodied voice-interaction model for children rather than the drill-and-response of most of the era's talking toys.

deepDive.heading: The audio-mixer music mode
deepDive.text: In music programs the child can add or remove individual instruments from the backing track, effectively mixing the arrangement by pushing buttons. This is a toy-scale audio mixer, an early and unusual way to give a child hands-on control over a multi-part audio composition.

deepDive.heading: Why it matters
deepDive.text: The Talk 'n Play belongs alongside the museum's voice- and audio-interaction entries (Speak & Spell, talking toys, early synthesis for kids) but stands apart by making the child a recording participant and a mixer, not just a responder.
